steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: No good.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: At the triplets... No, throughout this entire piece.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I thought you were trying to show off at first, but after a few sessions, it's clear that you're not. Instead, you're deliberately handling high-difficulty passages with excessive flair as if to obfuscate the less-technical passages.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: In theory, you should already be quite familiar with this piece, so what's the point of fudging the easy sections?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: The point...? To fudge my way out of this rote, mechanical drilling. How's that for an answer?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: You've lost your temper?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Showing off? Fudging? Why such loaded words?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: The way I see it, I'm wasting time repeating the same piece over and over.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Whether you understand or not doesn't matter to me, but you're going to be playing in MY concert. If I say it's no good, then that means it's no good.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Keep practicing. And don't stop until you understand what I'm talking about.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Fine. I also happen to want to know what manner of unfathomable creature I'm running from.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Start from measure seventeen. One, two, three, four...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: What's the matter?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: What was going through your head when you played that passage just now?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Nothing in particular.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Wrong.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: You're throwing a fit at me.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: And what warranted you specifically pointing that out to me?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: That was the best you've sounded all day.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Are you joking?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Do I need to joke around with you?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: All you can think about right now is how to shut me up, isn't that right?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: That's exactly the way to approach it. When I wrote this piece, I was also thinking of someone who always competes with me.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: You're not saying anything, so I assume you're still surly?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Or do you have such a problem with me that you don't want anything to do with me anymore?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: No, I actually thought...

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Thought what?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: (Takes a deep breath)

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: ––I thought you had a problem with me.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I do have a problem with you.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You have a problem with me... And is it that I'm a noble?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: That is one reason, but not a particularly important one.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: It's true that I do not like nobles, but that does not stop me from applauding their music.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Just as some nobles see me as unclean, but that does not stop them from practicing my compositions at home.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Even the fortunate ones, sheltered and blissfully unaware of the plight of man, with sufficient respect for music and a desire to pursue it, may be found expounding the joys of life.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: But your performance is virtuosic at times yet perfunctory at others. Overall, it's as if...

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: One side of you is just trying to kill time while the other half is going to great lengths for embellishments and frills, as if to prove to others that your problem is a matter of motivation rather than capacity.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Let me be clear about this– this is a form of blasphemy against music, an attitude I absolutely cannot accept.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Fortunately for you, you've already proven to me that you're not doing it on purpose.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: At least, you have the ability to rid yourself of this state.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: What I suspect more now is that you had a talented teacher who was irresponsible toward his students.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Yes, that's exactly the kind of person my teacher was.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Thanks to him, I can perform a few pieces on pretty much every instrument, but I loathe him from the bottom of my heart.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: If that actually is the case, his music must've been quite unusual as well.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You're right about that, but I don't want to talk about him anymore.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: No matter.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Back on topic. I need you to remember how you felt today.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I'm not telling you to keep holding your nose while you practice this piece. But I'd like you to remember the rhythms and expressions from this last time, and the way you played those passages and transitions.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Good, let's wrap things up. You must be tired from practicing for so long.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I still need to take a look around the concert hall and meet with my sponsor, so I need to get going soon.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: That's it for today. I'll have Ursula fetch something to drink for you and Kreide.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Ursula––

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Ursula, where are you?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Kreide? Have you seen Ursula?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: She said she was going to Rhodes Island to fetch some medicine, and left about half an hour ago.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Half an hour ago? Their office isn't that far away.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I'll head down to the Rhodes Island office to see what's going on. You two can go home.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: I was also about to go there to visit my grandpa, so I'll come with you.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Ebenholz, want to join us?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Not like I have anything better to do.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Ebenholz, Kreide, and Mr. Czerny too!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: You all came at just the right time. I'm cooking up some food. Would you like to join us in a bit?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Hibiscus, where's Ursula?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Ms. Ursula's helping out in the kitchen––

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Well if it isn't Herr Czerny.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Didn't you come here to pick up medicine? How'd you end up cooking?

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: That was the plan, but I caught Hibiscus cookin' and Andante went out again. Thought it'd be bad to impose, and offered to lend a hand. Now you're here and that takes care of tonight's dinner as well.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Since Ebenholz and Kreide are here too, we need to make extra.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: How about Grandpa's portion?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Your grandpa has been asleep this whole time. I'm afraid he won't be able to join us at the table tonight.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: The whole time...? Has his condition worsened?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Don't worry. As far as I can tell, that's a common side effect of the medication, but he'll adjust to it soon enough.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Alright...

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Hibiscus, what's this thing? It looks just like an apple.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: It's a very nutritious tuber, great for your health. I haven't seasoned it yet though, so hold on a bit.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Weren't you going to go check out the concert hall with your sponsor?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I still have to fill up the tank before I go.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: That sponsor must be very dear to you. Right, Herr Czerny?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Dear, huh... Hah, quite the opposite.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: At first, I truly thought the two of us kindred spirits. But I quickly realized she is not the same kind of person as I.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: If I recall correctly, your true soul mate was the one intimately connected to 'Morgen und Abend,' only to pass away before you completed that opus.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: That's right.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Now that I think about it more calmly, the reason you rubbed me the wrong way from the very beginning... might have something to do with the way this piece came about.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Hearing you play 'Morgen und Abend' like that filled my heart with some dissatisfaction.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: But now that you've seen the light, the stone in my heart has at last been shed.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: It's all thanks to all those hours of intense instruction you provided. Otherwise––Ugh.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I see sarcasm is also one of your bad habits?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Maybe it is.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: It's fine. I don't mind.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: The way I see it, the most important quality a musician can have... is sincerity.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Sarcasm aside, even deeply-rooted hatred, if expressed using the proper techniques, is meaningful all the same.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: The last dish is ready!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: If not for Ursula's help, cooking all these dishes would've taken forever.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Eating together makes it feel like we're one big family.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: (Mumbles) Family, huh...

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Speaking of family, I wonder how Lava is doing back on the landship...

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Lava?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Lava is my sister, and an Infected. She can be a handful at times, but she's a good egg.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Your eyes lighted up when you mentioned your sister, Hibiscus.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Eh, really? Heehee.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Lava's the kind of girl who remembers who's been good to her, even if she's bad at expressing it. She's always getting into trouble.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: She's also Infected, but unlike me, she's really into studying her own Originium Arts. That's why she needs to pay extra attention to her diet.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Plus, she tends to miss meals or stay up too late because of her training, and I always have to remind her––

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Oh my, I'm sorry. Whenever I talk about Lava, I can't help myself...

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: The food's going to go cold, so let's dig in! I'm going to go change Kreide's grandpa's bandages first, and then I'll be right back.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: She sure loves her little sister.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: That's what siblings are for.

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Can't help but wonder at times, if Mein Herr had a brother or sister of his own, maybe he'd be a bit more easygoing.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Ursula!

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Haha.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Hibiscus, are you done changing his bandages?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I'll be there in a moment––

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Coming, coming! Thanks for waiting!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Now then, don't stand on ceremony, go ahead and dig in!

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: Here you go, one order of pan-fried sauerkraut!

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Finally, something normal to eat.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Wait, huh? You even packed some of her 'health food' to go?!

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: I must admit the taste was rather odd, but I don't think it's good to waste food.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You can eat that yourself tomorrow!

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Care for another bowl of soup, Mein Herr?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: No thanks... I'm full.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: You didn't notice anything off with her cooking, when you were in the kitchen?

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Couldn't just go around tasting food, being in someone else's kitchen and all.

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Besides, she does cook plenty healthy, I could see that much.

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: S'pose I could also learn a thing or two from Hibiscus, change up m'own cookin'...

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Ah, Mein Herr, I'm just jokin', come back––

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: I'm back!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: How was it? Have you eaten yet? If not––

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: ––Thanks for the offer! But I already ate out!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Aw, I even saved a portion just for you.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Sorry for making you do the detective legwork, but it's hard for me to get around right now.

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: Don't worry about it. I'm also a part of the Afterglow. If I can find some way to improve the situation, it'll benefit me just fine.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Now for the data analysis...

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I must say, this setup surpasses my expectations.

steps.name: Frivolous Noble
steps.text: Far from it, Mein Herr.

steps.name: Frivolous Noble
steps.text: This is your farewell concert after all. If anything, it ought to be more grandiose.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I was talking about the instruments.

steps.name: Frivolous Noble
steps.text: Ah, yes. Dame Gertrude spent a significant amount of money procuring the highest-quality instruments. We've tried our best to meet you and your musicians' needs when it comes to the venue and equipment.

steps.name: Frivolous Noble
steps.text: Now that you've had a good look around...

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: If I'm not mistaken, I believe I still haven't seen the lounge?

steps.name: Frivolous Noble
steps.text: Ah, look at this sorry memory of mine.

steps.name: Frivolous Noble
steps.text: Right this way.

steps.name: Frivolous Noble
steps.text: That's strange, why won't this door open?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Is there someone inside?
Yes. Someone indeed is inside.

steps.name: Frivolous Noble
steps.text: Dame Gertrude?

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Considering the significance of this concert, I am personally inspecting the concert hall's furnishings.

steps.name: Frivolous Noble
steps.text: That you would have to come handle such trivial matters in person means that we have failed in our duties! Sincerest apologies!

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: It's fine.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: If I heard right, Herr Czerny is also here?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Yes, I am. What are you doing in there?

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: I'm checking the lounge's interior.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: In my opinion, while the lounge does meet the bare minimum as set by you and your musicians, it leaves much to be desired.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: (Sighs audibly)

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Water stains on the mirrors, rusting on the drawer handles' plating, small holes in the carpet, just to name a few of the problems...

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I told you before, this concert doesn't need so much pomp and flair. As long as things work, it's good enough.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: That will not do. As your sponsor, my reputation is closely tied to the performance that you and your underlings put on.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: How many times do I have to tell you, they are musicians who've volunteered to play in the concert, not my 'underlings!'

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: There is no difference in the eyes of the people you've invited.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Have it your way.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: I'll open the door for you now. You're free to inspect the facilities yourself.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Never mind, I'll just leave it in your hands.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Do you not want to come in and take a look?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Not in the slightest, so you can stop putting on airs.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I trust you didn't want to see my face either, right? So let's make things easy for one another.

steps.name: Frivolous Noble
steps.text: (Whispers) Herr Czerny, your tone...

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: This is how we've always talked to each other.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Then run along and do as you please. I'll proceed with the needed inspections here.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: I just hope that these mundane affairs will prove to be a benefit to you on the day of the concert, rather than a hindrance.
